audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called every stage 'Skill' up to two items, flattening a lane that has a clean Orianna level 1 and a clear Lux window at 4-5. The content layer and the packet chart agree on that shape and the full layer contradicted both.
audit.why: Kit-grounded: at level 1 Lux has one damage spell and no root setup. By 4-5 Light Binding reaches 1175 — further than anything you own — and a landed root chains Lucent Singularity plus the Illumination auto onto a champion with no dash.
audit.corrected: phases[0] moved to Orianna and phases[3] to Lux, each with its why rewritten to argue the new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes claimed 'level 6 doubles your lane presence' and 'Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar' — a magnitude with no source — while the content layer says 6 is even because Final Spark is a dodgeable skillshot.
audit.why: Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 and a committed skillshot; that is why 6 is even, and the page never said so.
audit.corrected: Spikes restated around Final Spark being a skillshot and Luden's matching her poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central claim about the matchup is WRONG. breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t all told the reader to 'minion-block' Light Binding and 'her combo never starts'. Riot's own text says the sphere binds up to two enemy units, so one minion in the line does not stop it reaching you.
audit.why: This is the advice a reader acts on before every step forward. Standing behind a single minion believing you are safe is worse than having no rule at all.
audit.corrected: All three now state the two-unit behaviour and tell you to sidestep rather than hide behind one minion.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lux.json (Q text: 'binds and deals damage to up to two enemy units')

audit.why: 49.16% over 2331 games, matching the brief's games field.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (catalogue defect 3), and dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' off Light Binding, which is a flat 10s at every rank.
audit.why: Five invented seconds is five seconds of standing in her range believing the root is down.
audit.corrected: 10s flat stated in cooldowns, winCon, tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Illumination was never mentioned. The brief flags it as an auto-attack reset, but Riot's text does not describe a reset — her damaging spells charge the target and her NEXT ATTACK ignites it for bonus damage. That is an on-hit detonation, not an attack-timer reset.
audit.why: The actionable fact is the same shape but not the same mechanic: after any spell lands on you, her auto is worth extra, so the answer is leaving auto range rather than watching for a reset animation. I wrote the version Riot's text supports and did not repeat the reset claim.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now states the mark-then-auto pattern and the step-out answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lux is called 'he/his/him' in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, five phases[].why, four dosFull/dontsFull titles and bodies, and two report entries — while the content layer correctly says 'her'.
dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted under a title about not burning R defensively — catalogue defect 2.
audit.why: Neither body answered its title, and the don't is the one place the 9s Command: Protect versus 110s Shockwave contrast belongs.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles with real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization named Zed as the Zhonya's trigger in a Lux matchup.
audit.corrected: Zhonya's keyed to Final Spark; magic resist justified by the fact her whole kit is magic damage.

notes: The most important fix on this page is not a template: three separate fields told the reader to 'minion-block' Light Binding and that 'her combo never starts'. Riot's text says the sphere binds up to two enemy units, so a single minion in the line does not stop it — a reader following that rule stands still and gets rooted. Corrected in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t. Second, dosFull[2].d promised a 'fifteen-second invitation' off an ability that is a flat 10s at every rank. DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE, reported per the brief's rule: the kit tags Lux's passive autoReset 'auto-attack reset — burst timing tell', and the brief's missingInteraction repeats it, but Riot's text describes Illumination as spells charging the target so her NEXT ATTACK ignites it for bonus damage — an on-hit detonation, not an attack-timer reset. I wrote the mark-then-auto version the text supports and did not repeat the reset claim. Chart: win[] and the packet levelChart agreed exactly; phases[].side disagreed on rows 0 and 3 only, both moved with their whys rewritten. Content layer left untouched — see unverified for the one claim in it I could not check.
